body_en_plain:
M O R E   M A I L ! !

         September, 1992

                     Page Reply

 How to write to us...02     -
 Stuart Burton........03    05
 Peter Bell...........06    10
 Dave Marriott........12     -
 Timothy Wilkins......16    17
 Brian Cavers.........18     -
 Alan Cox.............21    50
 Paul Hooper..........56     -
 John Saunders........58    60

   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From: Stuart Burton, POOLE,

Dear Sir,

I enclose cheque for `3.00 and
my original "OUTWRITE!" disc for
upgrade to the new version.
Incidentally, I have other SAM
word processing programs but
find "OUTWRITE!" is the easiest
to use.

I have just bought an excellent
monitor (PHILIPS model 8833 also
known as CM11342/05G)which gives
an excellent picture except that
it shows up a problem with my
SAM - namely, ghosting. Please
can you recommend a firm able to
do the small modification to my
SAM. The monitor is on special

offer from DIAMOND COMPUTER
SYSTEMS. I bought mine from the
POOLE branch TEL (0202)716226
for under `190.00 without leads
and had the leads made up for
`7.00 by D.J.ELECTRONICS in
Bournemouth TEL(0202)515073 who
will supply them for `8.00
including postage and packing.

        Yours sincerely,

         Stuart Burton

Brian Cavers to Stuart Burton

Cliff Jackson gives details of a
modification to stop "ghosting"
when the 8833 monitor is used on
a SAM in last month's OUTLETTERS
(Part 1). If you don't feel you
are confident enough to do the
work yourself and you don't know
anyone who can do it for you
then why not contact Bruce
Gordon (see LOOKOUT this month).
He may be willing to do the mod
or you may get a local TV repair
company to do it if you print
out Cliff's information and show
it to them.
                          Brian

From: Peter Bell,SHOREHAM BY SEA

At last you seem to have a
version of OUTWRITE! that would
satisfy me. To date I have seen
no WP program for SAM or
Spectrum that has come up to the
standard of TASWORD+2.

One major point was auto insert,
which inserted one or more
characters at the cursor, re-
justifying ahead as they were
typed in, and the reverse when
deleting. A second was that one
could alter the margins, press
reformat and the text would
realign to the new settings.
Also, better than TASWORD3, it
went back to the disc only to
LOAD and SAVE.

You now apparently have those
options, and others as well.
Therefore please find enclosed a
cheque for OUTWRITE v2.

You can tell I have version 1.2,
but I paid for it in kind
instead of cash, having been
asked to review the pre-release
and release copies, in
conjunction with Frank Harrop,
for the SAM SUPPLEMENT Club.
I've never used it since, as I
preferred going back to my
Spec+2(grey) and Tas+2, which
was more user friendly. Also,
with Qualitas+ merged in,

I can use my own "handwriting"
font, which I have named
"Samskrit", (and copyrighted).

Using Qualitas+ is the only way
I know of getting double height
print from my Amstrad DMP3000
printer, and then that is done
by double pass printing. Do you
know of any way it can be done
with OUTWRITE?

You've included a spell checker,
I see. I'm not sure that one is
as good as it sounds, for often
I come across errors which are
not spelling mistakes, but
mis-used words. e.g., "except"
instead of "accept"; "pacific"
instead of "specific". (Or
"wither" instead of "whither",
see Lookout pg 3, tho' wither is
what PBT has done!) The spell-
checker would pass them, as they
are not mis-spelled.

Sorry for picking up your error,
but you so rarely make one, I
couldn't let it go.

Regarding the future of OUTLET,
as an OAP I would rather not
have to pay extra for a disc,
but until the day that I have to
start eating into my capital, I
wouldn't like to miss a one. I
own all you have issued, except
a couple that weren't on disc.
Bit of a pest trying to find
room to stow them. Don't reduce
the frequency. You might like to
know that there are a number of
adverts around for books on how
to make money at home from your
computer! Either that or send
the other one out to work.
All the best, anyway.    - Peter

Brian Cavers to Peter Bell


Thanks, Peter.

OUTWRITE 2 has a line insert NOT
a character-by-character insert.
It is the same as in Version 1.
It does have variable margins
and can reform text within the
margins whether narrower or
wider and also has a simple cut
and paste option to "grab" a
paragraph and re-print it in a
separate column of any valid
width.

No, you cannot get double height
printouts with OUTWRITE except
on printers that accept the
double height command.

I agree about spellcheckers. I
believe there are very advanced
(and very expensive) ones on
the PC which can check grammar
and would know if a word like
"except" was used incorrectly
but the OUTWRITE spellchecker is
just to check for and challenge
words not in its dictionary. It
is most certainly not foolproof
but, believe me, the 512K dict-
ionary certainly spots most of
the errors in letters sent in to
OUTLETTERS! Of course, once
everyone has a copy of OUTWRITE
Version 2 then they can check
their own spelling and we shall
not need to (ahem!).

                      - Brian

From: D. Marriott, NOTTINGHAM




Dear Ron & Brian,

In response to your editorial in
Issue 60 - speaking for myself,
I wouldn't mind a price increase
if it ensured the survival of
OUTLET, and I don't think many
people would moan about the idea
of suspending payments for
contributions unless specific-
ally requested. I'm sure that
for most of us, having our
humble efforts deemed worthy of
publication and sharing with
other readers is at least as
much reward as the payments!

I like the idea of a reduced
rate, available specifically on
request by those who genuinely
cannot afford the full price; I
don't think many people would
try to pull a fast one on you
just to save a few quid, even in
the current economic climate.

Hopefully, we all realise the
benefits OUTLET has provided and
continues to provide - if it
wasn't for OUTLET, for example,
there'd have been no "OUTWRITE!"
and we'd all stttill bbe
ttryyingg to ttype with
Tasword... (and if I'd used my
brain I'd have ordered OUTWRITE!
2 before writing this letter, or
used the pre-production copy you
sent me, and used 32-column

margins so you didn't have to
re-edit it. Sorry, I'll remember
next time...). Whatever you do,
though, please don't decrease
the frequency of OUTLET!

Onto the problem of a program
that will accept a Variable name
in an Input statement and
display the relevant Variable,
this is no great hassle if you
use KEYIN:

    10 INPUT "Variable Name? ";x
    20 KEYIN "PRINT "+xx$

You'd probably want some error-
trapping in case a non-existent
Variable-name was entered, and
yes, it would still corrupt
"xx$" if that was what you
wanted to look at.

Another use of KEYIN that has
occurred to me, incidentally, is
to hold MasterDos or MasterBasic
statements in a program that
might be loaded under SamDos;
otherwise you can get garbage in
the program listing, and even if
you then boot in the right
system file, it might not be
able to recognise the commands.


        Yours Sincerely,

         Dave Marriott

From:T. Wilkins, GLOUCESTERSHIRE

Dear Chezron Software,

When do you expect Issue 2 of
The Style Writer to be finished,
fully tested and ready for SAM
Coupe owners? (I already have
Issue 1). I wrote to the
programmer of The Style Writer
and he said that he has nearly
finished Issue 2 but that you at
OUTLET will let your readers
know as soon as it is available.

I would be interested in updat-
ing my Issue of The Style Writer
as soon as Issue 2 becomes
available.

                    T. Wilkins

Brian Cavers to Timothy Wilkins

Sorry,I do not know when the new
STYLEWRITER will be ready. We do
not like to forecast or predict
until we know for certain as it
disappoints too many people.
Remember, Prince of Persia?
SAMCo announced it about June or
July and it was issued about
November!

Last month we announced OUTWRITE
2 could be ordered but allow 28
days for delivery in the first
month. It is right on target. I
am writing this at the end of
August;the master disc is ready;
the manual is written and in the
process of being re-checked then
printed.
                        - Brian

Brian Cavers to All

Cliff Jackson wrote in inquiring
about the new OUTWRITE asking if
the printer reset before prints
could be disabled so he could
use the control panel on his
printer. I have now found the
POKEs for this so I suggest that
anyone interested jot them down.

 DISABLE RESET BEFORE PRINTING:

   POKE 74876,0: POKE 74879,0

DISABLE RESET BEFORE "ANOTHER
COPY?" MESSAGE (ONLY OCCURS IN
NON-CONTINUOUS,I.E. SINGLE SHEET
PRINTING):

   POKE 75062,0: POKE 75066,0

I also found another place in
the code where the printer is
reset but could not see that it
affected anything. Obviously it
must do somewhere so you may
care to note these down too but
only use them if you find
another routine resetting the
printer when you don't want it
to!
   POKE 74823, 0: POKE 74826,0

Remember, all these POKEs are
only for the NEW version of
OUTWRITE, Version 2.0 and should
not be used on earlier versions.

Version 2 should be published by
the time you read this but if
not then it can only be a few
days before orders go out.

On a completely different topic,
when copying discs using two
drives it happens now and again
that a bad disc will trigger a
track/sector error message. The
problem is one cannot tell on
which disc the error occurred.
Here are some PEEKs that reveal
the last drive used on a SAM
(NOT the same as CURRENT drive).

    SAMDOS 20: PEEK DVAR 14202

 MASTERDOS 23: PEEK DVAR 14827
                       OR
               PEEK (DVAR 0-234)

I don't know if these MASTERDOS
peeks are the same on other
versions than Version 23 above.

                        - Brian

From: Alan D. Cox, DYFED

Dear Brian,

You will note that I have
reverted to Wordmaster (WM) for
this (and all subsequent)
aetters. I really did try to
come to grips with TASWORD (TW),
but it is so pathetic when
compared to WM that I cannot
bear to use it: I am amazed that
TW ever became the standard WP
for Spectrums - it must be a
triumph of history over common
sense. OK, all I am really
trying to say is that WM suits
me, and TW does not! At the risk
of boring you, the most pathetic
feature of TW is its so-called
insert mode.

Whoever programmed this did not
know what an insert mode should
do: in WM suppose I type in
'TASWORD is marvellous', and
then realise that I have omitted
'not'. All I do is to put the
cursor on the 'm ' of 'marvell-
ous' and then type in not+space
- all done, no messing about
with CNTRL I beforehand then
reformatting afterwards. Of
course, WM does not bother with
on-screen justification, which
no doubt makes things easier,
but I have never seen the point
of this - all I want is
justified printer output, and WM
does this easily. The insert
mode in QUILL, the WP that PSION
wrote for the QL, also works in
this way.

Other irritating features are
the need to go back to a
separate menu to select major
functions - WM has on-screen
menus - and the need to confirm
all the time - much better to
have an ESC capability if errors
are made, which is rarely, I
guess. In addition, when I ask
to SAVE in WM, it offers me a
name that is either the one I
used when I created a new file,
or else the same as I used in a
previous GET or SAVE: TW just
gives me a DIR! I rest my case.

Sadly, OUTWRITE! version 1
appears to share these same
faults, although I read into
your comments that version 2
gets over some of them.

But does it have a proper insert
mode? - if it does then I might
convert to it, assuming that you
can accept it as a standard, but
otherwise not.

I am still not clear exactly
what you do with my WM files to
make them useful in your system.
Would it help if I sent you an
ASCII file, where all the
command lines, special
characters and underlines are
removed?

Turning now to other matters, it
gives me no pleasure to say 'I
told you so' about the sorry
business of SAMCo being in the
hands of a liquidator, but I saw
this coming, as you know.

I am aware of the effort being
made by West Coast Computers
(never heard of them - have
you?) to mount a rescue package
for SAM, not SAMCo, but I have
to say that I cannot believe
that SAM has a viable commercial
future in this country - perhaps
things may be different in
countries that have a less
sophisticated background in
computer matters, but even then
I have my doubts.

What I believe should happen is
that a SAM Owners Club should be
set up to safeguard as far as is
possible the interests of those
of us who have already invested
money and intellectual effort in
SAM. In particular, if there are


any replacement parts with the
liquidator (or with the receiver
for MGT) that would enable
repairs to continue to be
carried out (although clearly
not by PBT, in view of your
comments!) then they should be
bought on behalf of existing
owners. I have made these points
to Bob Brenchley, who is acting
as the interface between West
Coast Computers and interested
SAM owners.

I am not sure that I fully
understand the aim of Malcolm
Goodman's puzzle: why not just
PRINT x? However, one problem
you had with your solution was
that you destroyed the variable
you were after (or its partner)

by naming it in an INPUT state-
ment. I could not see any way to
get round this using INKEY$, and
the only thought I had was to
get the required symbol into the
BASIC via an on-screen menu. The
following is a listing of a
Spectrum program that deals with
numerical variables - and the
extension to string variabes is
fairly obvious (and is left as
an exercise for the reader!)

   1 GO SUB 1000
   9 PRINT AT 0,0;"NUMBERS"
  10 FOR m=0 TO 12
  12 PRINT AT 1,M;CHR$ (97+m);AT
     2,m;CHR$ (110+m);
  30 NEXT m
 100 LET rr=1: LET cc=0
 105 LET rrr=rr: LET ccc=cc

 110 PRINT OVER 1;AT rr,cc;CHR$
     143
 120 LET rr=rr+(INKEY$="6" AND
     rr=1)-(INKEY$="7" AND rr=2)
 121 LET cc=cc+(INKEY$="8" AND
     cc<12)-(INKEY$="S" and
     CC>0)
 123 IF INKEY$="0" THEN GO TO
        130
 124 PRINT OVER 1;AT rrr,ccc;
     CHR$ 143
 125 PAUSE 20: GO TO 105
 130 PRINT AT 10,0;
     VAL SCREEN$(rr,cc)
 999 STOP
1010 LET nn=1
1020 LET zz=PEEK 23637+256*PEEK
     23638: POKE (zz+5),(96+nn)
1030 LET z=nn
1040 LET nn=nn+1
1050 IF nn<=26 THEN GO TO 1020
1060 RETURN

It is, as usual with my prog-
rams, somewhat lengthy, but at
least I enjoyed writing it. As I
do not have my Disciple at pres-
ent, I have to use Interface 1,
and the only serial printer that
I have is the Tandy CGP115,
which explains the somewhat odd
printing: if this happens again
in the future do you still
accept programs on microdrive
cassettes? - which I would want
back, of course!

On the general point, I would be
interested to see programming
problems in OUTLET, although I
doubt I would send you many
solutions - I am a problem
solver, not a programmer, by
nature. The sort of thing I have


in mind is shown by the sub-
routine at 1010 - how simply to
set the variables a to z equal
to 1 to 26? - the method I have
used, with N XTLIN, has already
been published, for strings, in
FORMAT.
I tried out the DTRANS programs
that you sent me. Normally they
worked well, but occasionally I
get some funny looking outputs.
On investigation, these were
where DTRANS had translated
things like DEF FN B(T)=INT VAL
"F/(PEEK(C+12+T) +PEEK(C+13+T)
*256 +2)+.5" where because I
think of the odd (to me)
convention about things inside
inverted commas, you get an
incomprehensible symbol instead
of PEEK.

The programs worked OK, but are
not readable. I found a way
around this: if you really want
to know what the program says,
EDIT the line in question and
then DELETE the first inverted
commas. The interpreter then
goes back to e.g. PEEK and all
is comprehensible. If you want a
tidy looking program you can jot
down the unquotes information
and type it in in stead. Or can
you think of a simple way to do
this automatically?

Two other thoughts, inspired to
some extent by my current
activities. First, I find DTRANS
useful, but since I prefer to
program in SAMBASIC but would
like to offer you programs for

both machines when possible, I
would find a 'Reverse DTRANS'
very useful i.e. something that
would translate a SAMBASIC
program into Spectrum BASIC. I
know it is not as straight-
forward as DTRANS, since whereas
any Spectrum BASIC line has a
SAM equivalent, the reverse is
not the case, so some sort of
'error checking' would be
needed. A challenge to your
machine-code-literate readers!
Secondly, whilst I find
SAMBASIC's RENUM command very
useful, my sloppy programming
style means that I would often
like to renumber a block of code
in the middle of a program in
such a way that it would then
appear in a different place in

the program-as a simple example,
renumber lines 40 to 70 in a
program comprising lines 10 to
100 so that the block in
question then appears as lines
110 to 140. As far as I know,
RENUM cannot do this. However,
it is trivial, albeit tiresome,
to do it manually in BASIC viz
EDIT first line, alter its line
number, ENTER it, DELETE it at
its original line number, then
repeat for all other lines in
the block of interest. I believe
that anything that I can do in
BASIC can also be done using
machine code - after all, that
is what BASIC is using. Can any
of your readers, with greater
skills in machine code than I
shall ever acquire write a bit
of code to do this job?

A few comments on issue 60:
(i) Re: your financial problems.
I am content with your proposals
I do not know enough about your
business to know how much you
spend on postage to return disks
to people that send them to you,
but in some ways it seems a bit
of a waste - the postage could
equal the value of the disk. If
I know that you are not going to
return my disk, it is no great
sweat to keep a copy of what I
send you (I normally do in any
case). Of course, if you keep my
disk you owe me a bit of money:
would it be administratively
complicated to credit me with
the value of the disks you keep
and either deduct it from my
next years sub, or else send me
a cheque once a year?.

You could do this on a nominal
value per disk based on what you
could get for them -I pay 40p
each, but no doubt they are not
worth that to you.Only a thought
- what do you think? Yet another
thought - why do you offer a
reduced rate for subs - I use
the system for convenience,
rather than to save money.

(ii) I know it is, and will
continue to be, a problem for
you, but I hope that you will
not be publishing too many
programs that need MasterBASIC
or MasterDOS - as a a matter of
policy I think that you should
aim for the lowest common
multiplier among your readers,
and until MB and MD are 'in the


public domain' - one task for
the SAM Owners Club I mention
above would be to buy out Andy
Wright's interests in these two
programs so that they are
available to all SAM owners - I
think they should generally be
avoided. In fact, although I
have MasterBASIC (but not Master
DOS)I rarely use it since I hope
to send you some of my stuff and
therefore want it to work with
SAMBASIC (except when it is
possible to write for both at
the same time),(and Spectrum
too, if possible) and also there
is the problem of making sure
that I do not inadvertently send
someone who has not bought it a
disk with MasterBASIC on it.


(iii) I was interested in
D.A.Turton's program "Addprint"
for printing addresses on (both
sides of)envelopes.In my exper-
ience the really difficult bit
of printing on envelopes is get-
ting the printer mechanism to
hold and control the envelope
itself, because there is not
enough paper to grip. One part-
ial solution to this is to put
the envelope into the printer
sideways on, so that there is
more for the printer to grasp.
You then need a program to print
the address sideways, of course,
and there was one by Dave
Kennedy in FORMAT Vol 2, No 1,
August 1988.This is very effect-
ive - I even got it to work on
my Brother HR5! Clearly it is

FORMAT copyright, so I cannot
send it to you, but Bob
Brenchley can supply copies of
all back numbers, although for
Vols 1 to 3 only in complete
volumes, Vol 1 at `10 and Vols 2
and 3 at `12. An alternative, if
you have a tractor feed on your
printer, is to use tractor feed
labels - or even tractor feed
envelopes, although those I have
seen are very expensive.

(iv) You may, if you wish, cont-
inue to believe in the existence
of a centrifugal force, but I
think you should explain what
causes it!
(v) I note the letter from
Malcolm Forbes in Add-enders 3
about wordprocessors.

I have a copy of 'The Last Word'
on cassette but easily transfer-
able to disk (or at least it was
on my Disciple) - and I would be
happy to donate this to him if
you or he would send me his
address. However, as I have made
clear earlier on, in my view
'WORDMASTER' is the best word
processor around and I would
strongly recommend it to Mr.
Forbes.

I note that you quote an address
for PCG - the latest information
I have is that they are now
trading as Polytype, with a week
day mornings phone number:

0229 832807 - information from
FORMAT July 1992.

(vi) Re: R. Webster's letter in
Addenders 4 - the only reference
I have in my database to a disk
drive for the ZX 81 is to a
"Floppy Disc Controller" advert-
ised by Analogue Information
Services - for example in ZX
Computing June/July 83. In view
of the date, this information is
offered merely to keep the
record straight.


(vii) When in the add-verts
section of Addenders the normal
B and F keys do not work. A
trivial point, and no doubt you
have many more important things
to do than sort this out, but I
make the point if only to show
that I do look at the ads!

(viii) In view of my comments
earlier on WPs, do you happen to
know whether 'The Style Writer'
has a "proper" insert mode? Even
if it does, since I do not have
512k, and with the present
situation I cannot just order
one up from SAMCo, it would only
be for information.

(ix) I was interested to read
Mike Pike's piece in Drive Chat
on viruses. Would you and/or he
have any objection to my arrang-
ing for it to be reproduced,
with full acknowledgements, of
course, in the Newsletter of the
Carmarthen Computer User Group?

Because of their heavy handed
attempts at humour, I never know

whether to take anything in
Spectrum User seriously. How-
ever, I should be interested to
know whether you or any of your
readers have any comments on the
following letter and response in
the July 1992 Specman column.

"128 SAM/SPEC"
Dear Specman, I own a SAM Coupe
and was wondering if it is
possible to get 128K programs
that were made for 128K Speccys
(yuk! - my comment: ADC) running
on it instead of the 48K progs
I'm limited to at the moment.

C.Reed, Abington

Thinking about it, and I'll bet
this is going to put the cat

among the pidgeons (sic), it is
possible to do this but the
games need a re-write of their
top code. The Coupe pages in
banks from 32768 to 65535
whereas the Spectrum does so in
banks from 49152 to 65535. So
what would you have to do for
the Coupe? Well, because it is
arranged that bank 3 5 7 9 etc
always fall at 32768 you will
have to put a copy of the code
from 32768 to 49151 in each of
these banks. Then copy the
normal 128K ROM banks onto 2 4
6 8, if you catch my drift. It
is a bit techie so don't try it
without knowing at least some-
thing about the workings of your
machine but if it's any consol-
ation I got it to work for a

128k game on my Coupe. Though it
took me two days to convert it!"
My first question is "do you
know what this means?" - I am
not being sarcastic, merely that
I am not clever enough to under-
stand it. I have always under-
stood that 'because the 128k
pages memory using hardware,
whereas SAM uses software'(not
meant to be an accurate quote)
it was not possible to emulate
the former on the latter - which
is effectively what C.Reed is
asking for (I think!).
Any comments?

I am sorry about the boob over
the position in memory of the
screen - one more boob and I
shall stop sending you material!

I sit here in my own little
world of 256k and only one disk
drive, and I tend to forget that
others have 512k and/or two
drives (although I do try to
remember that not everybody will
have MasterBASIC). It seems to
me that this is the sort of
point you might make in the
'Guide to Contributors' that I
proposed some while ago.

You may recall the debate on
calculating the date of Easter,
when I set out to sort it all
out and then found that I could
not. The problem has stayed on
my backburner, and whenever I
have had the chance I have
consulted colleagues. I have
been unable to trace the


original debate - was it in the
Spectrum version of OUTLET, or
have I overlooked it?I hope I am
not repeating things that have
gone before. A colleague, Tom
Ashmore, has given me two
algorithms to determine Easter
Day, the first being one that he
derived from the rules in the
Book of Common Prayer (BCP),
which is meant to work from 1600
to 2199,and the second a proced-
ure which claims to work from
1583 to any future date. I set
up a small program to compare
the two for the dates during
which the BCP algorithm claims
to work.The agreement was rem-
arkably good - the only differ-
ences were for 5 years in the
17th century and 2 in the 21st.

I do not have any independent
source for the 21st century, but
for the 17th century the Oxford
Companion to English Literature
gives the dates, and in each
case where there was a differ-
ence between the two algorithms,
the nonBCP one was correct. Thus
the evidence available suggests
to me that the best algorithm,
which has the additional
advantage that it is a
straightforward calculation,
with no 'correction factors'
involved, is the second one.
This is quoted in a book by
Peter Duffett-Smith called
"PRACTICAL ASTRONOMY WITH YOUR
CALCULATOR ", Cambridge
University Press, Second edition
1981 plus later re-prints.

Clearly the book itself is copy-
right,but the algorithm on which
my program is based is stated to
have been devised in 18 76 and
published in "Butcher's
Ecclesiastical Calendar", so
there cannot be any real
copyright problems with it.

The program follows (it could be
made a bit shorter at the
expense of clarity):

 10 INPUT "What year (1583
    onwards) ?;y
 20 LET a=y-19*INT(y/19)
 30 LET b=INT(y/100)
 40 LET c=y-100*b
 50 LET d=INT(b/4)
 60 LET e=b-4*d
 70 LET f=INT((b+ 8)/25)

 80 LET g=INT((b-f+1)/3)
 90 LET temp=INT(19*a+b- d-g+15)
100 LET h=temp-30*INT(temp/30)
110 LET i=INT(c/4 )
120 LET k=c-4*i
130 LET temp=32+2*e+2*i-h-k
140 LET l=temp-7*INT(temp/7)
150 LET temp=a+11*h+22*l
160 LET m=INT(temp/451)
170 LET temp=h+l-7*m+114
180 LET n=INT( temp/31)
190 LET p=temp-31*n
200 PRINT (p+1);" ";("March "
    AND n=3)+("April" AND n=4)
210 PAUSE 0:GOTO 10
If you had any doubts about the
correctness of this, no doubt
the occurrence of the constant
451 will reassure you!
All best wishes,
                    - Alan D.Cox

Brian Cavers to Alan Cox

Yes,I agree the character insert
mode in WORDMASTER is very good.

fore have a "proper" printing
routine. Many PC users with very
advanced word processors may be
so used to printing one document
while typing another that they
would be astonished that you
cannot use the wordprocessor
just because it is printing.

As far as sending us files,just
continue to send WM files as we
have a routine to strip out the
codes.

Returning contribution discs to
U.K. addresses costs nothing
because the postage is no more

letter. It does pain a bit to
pay `1 postage to return a disc
worth about 35p overseas! Yes,it
would be awkward to credit discs
instead of returning them.

We offer a reduced rate for
subscriptions because subs are
less work for us,give us advance
cash and commit the reader to a
term. Naturally we want to
encourage them by compensating
the reader in proportion.

I agree it is a shame MASTERDOS
and BASIC are not standard but
there are bound to be he odd one
or two in OUTLET.

If I see that the only reason a
program uses MD or MB can be
easily duplicated in SAMDOS I
would probably alter the program
but the best programs work under
either SAMDOS or the MASTERS but
HAVE EXTRA OPTIONS (or work

OUTWRITE is like this. It works
happily on any SAM but a 512K
machine can use a bigger spell-
ing dictionary; RAMDISCS, TIME,
DATE, SUBDIRECTORIES etc. may be
used if you MASTERDOS and print
spooling operates if you have
MASTERBASIC installed.

Centrifugal force is the force
caused by the kinetic energy in
a rotating body trying to keep
the mass of the body moving in a

straight line acting against a
constraint. If you spin a weight
on a cord around your body it
will be "forced"as far away from
you as the cord (and any other
constraints) will allow. Are you
saying that Physicists no longer
accept the term? I must be out
of touch! It's a long time since
I went to school! Why do experts
call the force "centrifugal" and
why are centrifuges so called?

Yes, it IS possible to have 128K
Spectrum programs running. We
have been sent some 128K games
that were converted in Europe.
They run perfectly,including the
128K music but I don't know of
any general-purpose Spectrum 128
emulator.

Yes, STYLEWRITER also has a
"proper" insert mode and it is a
line insert mode the same as
Tasword 2 and OUTWRITE - not a
character insert mode!

                      - Brian

From: Paul Hooper,
110, Westward Rise, BARRY, South
Glamorgan, South Wales CF6 8PQ

First of all, a SHOCK .... My

1 GO SUB 1000 9 PRINT AT 0,0;"NUMBERS" 10 FOR m=0 TO 12 12 PRINT AT 1,M;CHR$ (97+m);AT 2,m;CHR$ (110+m); 30 NEXT m 100 LET rr=1: LET cc=0 105 LET rrr=rr: LET ccc=cc

110 PRINT OVER 1;AT rr,cc;CHR$ 143 120 LET rr=rr+(INKEY$="6" AND rr=1)-(INKEY$="7" AND rr=2) 121 LET cc=cc+(INKEY$="8" AND cc<12)-(INKEY$="S" and

in mind is shown by the sub- routine at 1010 - how simply to set the variables a to z equal to 1 to 26? - the method I have used, with N XTLIN, has already been published, for strings, in FORMAT. Webster's letter in Addenders 4 - the only reference I have in my database to a disk drive for the ZX 81 is to a "Floppy Disc Controller" advert- ised by Analogue Information Services - for example in ZX Computing June/July 83. (vii) When in the add-verts section of Addenders the normal B and F keys do not work. A trivial point, and no doubt you have many more important things to do than sort this out, but I make the point if only to show that I do look at the ads!

Because of their heavy handed attempts at humour, I never know

"128 SAM/SPEC" Dear Specman, I own a SAM Coupe and was wondering if it is possible to get 128K programs that were made for 128K Speccys (yuk! - my comment: ADC) running on it instead of the 48K progs I'm limited to at the moment.

C.Reed, Abington

Thinking about it, and I'll bet this is going to put the cat

among the pidgeons (sic), it is possible to do this but the games need a re-write of their top code. The Coupe pages in banks from 32768 to 65535 whereas the Spectrum does so in banks from 49152 to 65535. So what would you have to do for the Coupe? Well, because it is arranged that bank 3 5 7 9 etc always fall at 32768 you will have to put a copy of the code from 32768 to 49151 in each of these banks. Then copy the normal 128K ROM banks onto 2 4 6 8, if you catch my drift. It is a bit techie so don't try it without knowing at least some- thing about the workings of your machine but if it's any consol- ation I got it to work for a

128k game on my Coupe. Though it took me two days to convert it!" My first question is "do you know what this means?" - I am not being sarcastic, merely that I am not clever enough to under- stand it. I have always under- stood that 'because the 128k pages memory using hardware, whereas SAM uses software'(not meant to be an accurate quote) it was not possible to emulate the former on the latter - which is effectively what C.Reed is asking for (I think!). Any comments?

I am sorry about the boob over the position in memory of the screen - one more boob and I shall stop sending you material!

I sit here in my own little world of 256k and only one disk drive, and I tend to forget that others have 512k and/or two drives (although I do try to remember that not everybody will have MasterBASIC). It seems to me that this is the sort of point you might make in the 'Guide to Contributors' that I proposed some while ago.

You may recall the debate on calculating the date of Easter, when I set out to sort it all out and then found that I could not. The problem has stayed on my backburner, and whenever I have had the chance I have consulted colleagues. I have been unable to trace the

original debate - was it in the Spectrum version of OUTLET, or have I overlooked it?I hope I am not repeating things that have gone before. A colleague, Tom Ashmore, has given me two algorithms to determine Easter Day, the first being one that he derived from the rules in the Book of Common Prayer (BCP), which is meant to work from 1600 to 2199,and the second a proced- ure which claims to work from 1583 to any future date. I set up a small program to compare the two for the dates during which the BCP algorithm claims to work.The agreement was rem- arkably good - the only differ- ences were for 5 years in the 17th century and 2 in the 21st.

I do not have any independent source for the 21st century, but for the 17th century the Oxford Companion to English Literature gives the dates, and in each case where there was a differ- ence between the two algorithms, the nonBCP one was correct. Thus the evidence available suggests to me that the best algorithm, which has the additional advantage that it is a straightforward calculation, with no 'correction factors' involved, is the second one. This is quoted in a book by Peter Duffett-Smith called "PRACTICAL ASTRONOMY WITH YOUR CALCULATOR ", Cambridge University Press, Second edition 1981 plus later re-prints.

Clearly the book itself is copy- right,but the algorithm on which my program is based is stated to have been devised in 18 76 and published in "Butcher's Ecclesiastical Calendar", so there cannot be any real copyright problems with it.

The program follows (it could be made a bit shorter at the expense of clarity):

10 INPUT "What year (1583 onwards) ?;y 20 LET a=y-19*INT(y/19) 30 LET b=INT(y/100) 40 LET c=y-100*b 50 LET d=INT(b/4) 60 LET e=b-4*d 70 LET f=INT((b+ 8)/25)

80 LET g=INT((b-f+1)/3) 90 LET temp=INT(19*a+b- d-g+15) 100 LET h=temp-30*INT(temp/30) 110 LET i=INT(c/4 ) 120 LET k=c-4*i 130 LET temp=32+2*e+2*i-h-k 140 LET l=temp-7*INT(temp/7) 150 LET temp=a+11*h+22*l 160 LET m=INT(temp/451) 170 LET temp=h+l-7*m+114 180 LET n=INT( temp/31) 190 LET p=temp-31*n 200 PRINT (p+1);" ";("March " AND n=3)+("April" AND n=4) 210 PAUSE 0:GOTO 10 If you had any doubts about the correctness of this, no doubt the occurrence of the constant 451 will reassure you! All best wishes, - Alan D.Cox

Brian Cavers to Alan Cox

Yes,I agree the character insert mode in WORDMASTER is very good. There are lots of other things to compare though. On the SAM for instance, the screen display is terrible compared to OUTWRITE because WM uses a Mode 1 screen whereas OW uses Mode 3. Did you check out the demo in OUTLET 51?

The implication that a line insert mode is somehow "wrong" or "improper" is unacceptable. Can you continue to type a new document in WORDMASTER while the last one is still printing? No. OUTWRITE can but I would not say that WORDMASTER does not there- fore have a "proper" printing routine. Many PC users with very advanced word processors may be so used to printing one document while typing another that they would be astonished that you cannot use the wordprocessor just because it is printing.

As far as sending us files,just continue to send WM files as we have a routine to strip out the codes.

Returning contribution discs to U.K. addresses costs nothing because the postage is no more if with the acknowledgement letter. It does pain a bit to pay `1 postage to return a disc worth about 35p overseas! Yes,it would be awkward to credit discs instead of returning them.

We offer a reduced rate for subscriptions because subs are less work for us,give us advance cash and commit the reader to a term. Naturally we want to encourage them by compensating the reader in proportion.

I agree it is a shame MASTERDOS and BASIC are not standard but there are bound to be he odd one or two in OUTLET.

If I see that the only reason a program uses MD or MB can be easily duplicated in SAMDOS I would probably alter the program but the best programs work under either SAMDOS or the MASTERS but HAVE EXTRA OPTIONS (or work better) using MD/MB. The new OUTWRITE is like this. It works happily on any SAM but a 512K machine can use a bigger spell- ing dictionary; RAMDISCS, TIME, DATE, SUBDIRECTORIES etc. may be used if you MASTERDOS and print spooling operates if you have MASTERBASIC installed.

Centrifugal force is the force caused by the kinetic energy in a rotating body trying to keep the mass of the body moving in a

straight line acting against a constraint. If you spin a weight on a cord around your body it will be "forced"as far away from you as the cord (and any other constraints) will allow. Are you saying that Physicists no longer accept the term? I must be out of touch! It's a long time since I went to school! Why do experts call the force "centrifugal" and why are centrifuges so called?

Yes, it IS possible to have 128K Spectrum programs running. We have been sent some 128K games that were converted in Europe. They run perfectly,including the 128K music but I don't know of any general-purpose Spectrum 128 emulator.

Yes, STYLEWRITER also has a "proper" insert mode and it is a line insert mode the same as Tasword 2 and OUTWRITE - not a character insert mode!

- Brian

First of all, a SHOCK .... My father has a Notebook PC which I am using to write this letter. I bought a PC magazine called PCPlus which had two discs taped to the front. **От:** Peter Bell, SHOREHAM BY SEA

Наконец-то у вас, похоже, появилась версия OUTWRITE!, способная меня удовлетворить. До сегодняшнего дня я не встречал ни одного текстового процессора для SAM или Spectrum, который дотягивал бы до уровня TASWORD+2.

Одним из главных достоинств была автоматическая вставка: вставка одного или нескольких символов в позиции курсора со сдвигом текста вперед по мере набора, и наоборот при удалении. Теперь у вас, судя по всему, есть эти возможности, а также некоторые другие. Поэтому, пожалуйста, примите прилагаемый чек за OUTWRITE v2.

Вы можете заметить, что у меня есть версия 1.2, но я заплатил за нее не деньгами, а услугой: меня попросили написать рецензию на предрелизную и релизную версии совместно с Frank Harrop для клуба SAM SUPPLEMENT. С тех пор я им ни разу не пользовался, предпочитая возвращаться к своему Spec+2 (серому) и Tas+2, который был более дружелюбен к пользователю. Например, «except» вместо «accept»; «pacific» вместо «specific». (Или «wither» вместо «whither», см. Lookout стр. 3, хотя «иссушение» — это как раз то, что произошло с PBT!).     10 INPUT "Variable Name? ";x
```text
    20 KEYIN "PRINT "+xx$
```

Искренне ваш,  
Dave Marriott

**От:** T. Wilkins, GLOUCESTERSHIRE

Когда вы планируете выпустить Issue 2 текстового процессора The Style Writer — полностью протестированным и готовым для владельцев SAM Coupe? (Issue 1 у меня уже есть). **Brian Cavers отвечает Timothy Wilkins:**

К сожалению, я не знаю, когда будет готов новый STYLEWRITER. Мы предпочитаем не давать прогнозов и предсказаний, пока не будем уверены на все сто, поскольку это разочаровывает слишком многих. Помните Prince of Persia? SAMCo анонсировала её примерно в июне или июле, а вышла она только около ноября!

                        — Brian

**Brian Cavers ко всем:**

Cliff Jackson написал нам по поводу нового OUTWRITE с вопросом: можно ли отключить сброс принтера перед печатью, чтобы он мог использовать панель управления на самом принтере? Я нашел нужные POKE, так что предлагаю всем заинтересованным их записать.

ОТКЛЮЧЕНИЕ СБРОСА ПЕРЕД ПЕЧАТЬЮ:

```text
   POKE 74876,0: POKE 74879,0
```

ОТКЛЮЧЕНИЕ СБРОСА ПЕРЕД СООБЩЕНИЕМ «ANOTHER COPY?» (ТОЛЬКО ПРИ ПОЛИСТОВОЙ ПЕЧАТИ, Т. Е. НЕ НЕПРЕРЫВНОЙ):

```text
   POKE 75062,0: POKE 75066,0
```

Я также нашел в коде еще одно место, где сбрасывается принтер, но не заметил, чтобы это на что-то влияло. Коллега, Tom Ashmore, дал мне два алгоритма для определения пасхального воскресенья: первый он вывел из правил «Книги общих молитв» (Book of Common Prayer — BCP), который должен работать с 1600 по 2199 год, а второй — процедура, заявляющая работоспособность с 1583 года до любой даты в будущем. Я написал небольшую программу, чтобы сравнить оба алгоритма на тех датах, для которых заявлена работа алгоритма BCP. Совпадение оказалось поразительно точным — расхождения возникли лишь за 5 лет в XVII веке и за 2 года в XXI.

У меня нет независимого источника для XXI века, но для XVII века даты дает Oxford Companion to English Literature, и во всех случаях, где между двумя алгоритмами была разница, верным оказывался вариант не по BCP. Таким образом, имеющиеся данные говорят мне о том, что лучшим алгоритмом — обладающим к тому же тем преимуществом, что он представляет собой прямой расчет без каких-либо «поправочных коэффициентов» — является второй вариант. Он цитируется в книге Peter Duffett-Smith под названием «PRACTICAL ASTRONOMY WITH YOUR CALCULATOR», Cambridge University Press, второе издание 1981 года плюс более поздние переиздания.

Разумеется, сама книга защищена авторским правом, но алгоритм, на котором основана моя программа, как утверждается, был разработан в 1876 году и опубликован в «Butcher's Ecclesiastical Calendar», так что с ним никаких реальных проблем с авторскими правами быть не может.

Ниже следует программа (ее можно было бы сделать чуть короче в ущерб понятности):

```text
 10 INPUT "What year (1583 onwards) ?";y
 20 LET a=y-19*INT(y/19)
 30 LET b=INT(y/100)
 40 LET c=y-100*b
 50 LET d=INT(b/4)
 60 LET e=b-4*d
 70 LET f=INT((b+8)/25)
 80 LET g=INT((b-f+1)/3)
 90 LET temp=INT(19*a+b-d-g+15)
100 LET h=temp-30*INT(temp/30)
110 LET i=INT(c/4)
120 LET k=c-4*i
130 LET temp=32+2*e+2*i-h-k
140 LET l=temp-7*INT(temp/7)
150 LET temp=a+11*h+22*l
160 LET m=INT(temp/451)
170 LET temp=h+l-7*m+114
180 LET n=INT(temp/31)
190 LET p=temp-31*n
200 PRINT (p+1);" ";("March " AND n=3)+("April " AND n=4)
210 PAUSE 0:GOTO 10
```

Если у вас были какие-то сомнения в правильности этого кода, то появление константы 451 наверняка вас успокоит!
С наилучшими пожеланиями,
